messages:
anil: seeing a weird one — nsys trace for a KV cache hotpath has no source lines for the runtime kernels when run inside the perf container, but host builds have lines. anyone seen this with nsight/CUPTI + container bind mounts?

chris: hm. which image and how are you running nsys? quick paste of the exact command and the docker run flags would help.

anil: reproduced with the repro image: `redwood/runtime-perf:kvcache-debug`
run: `docker run --rm -v /var/lib/debug:/usr/lib/debug:ro -v /proc:/hostproc:ro --privileged --pid=host 
  redwood/runtime-perf:kvcache-debug /bin/bash -c "nsys profile -o out -t cupti,cuda,osrt ./bin/serve --bench --trace"`

output snippet: 
```
nsys: collection complete, writing out: out.qdrep
nsys: ERROR: symbol lookup failed for /opt/runtime/lib/rt_kernels.so, no line info
```

sara: two quick suspects: (1) buildids differ between the binary in the container and the debug info on the host (path-mapping won't help), or (2) CUPTI/NSIGHT can't read inside chrooted/proc namespaces unless the tool is launched from host mount points.

mia: +1 for buildid mismatch. did you strip or do any post-processing in the image? also check `eu-readelf --notes` to compare Build ID.

anil: binary in image is unstripped (`-g` present) but we do run `objcopy --only-keep-debug` during packaging and ship debug separately into /var/lib/debug on the host. i had assumed bind-mount would be enough.

chris: try `llvm-objdump --syms` vs `readelf -n` inside container and on host debugfile to ensure they share the same buildid. if buildid doesn't match, perf/nsys will ignore the host debugfile.

anil: did that — host debug file buildid: `0b8f3d2a...` container so/dyn note: `0b8f3d2a...` — they match. still no lines.

sara: okay next: CUPTI activity reports device timelines but stitching to userland frames needs the tracer to resolve addresses using /proc/<pid>/maps. when pid namespaces are host, and you used `--pid=host` should be fine, but `--privileged` can change mount namespaces. can you run the same nsys command on the host (pointing to the container bin via bind) instead of inside container, i.e. run nsys from host and profile the container pid?

anil: ran host nsys and attached to container pid. new qdrep shows kernel timeline with user space frames, but all runtime frames are still missing source lines — they show `<unknown>` with addresses.

mia: do you have sourceless inline functions or LTO with stripped inline debug info? also check `-fno-omit-frame-pointer` at compile time — without frame pointers some stacks are impossible to unwind reliably for some tools.

anil: build flags include `-g -fno-omit-frame-pointer` and we don't use LTO for this build.

chris: another angle: CUPTI can generate separate activity records and sometimes nsys needs `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` exported in the traced process environment to associate GPU samples. also ensure the runtime was built with frame pointer support for optimized O3 kernels where frames are inlined.

anil: side note — i noticed `nsys` warnings: `Warning: QObject: CUPTI API registration failed: CUPTI_ERROR_NOT_INITIALIZED` during some runs where nsys didn't capture anything. but not reproducible.

sara: that warning is usually when CUPTI can't connect to driver due to driver mismatch or non-root container binding. are you using the same Nvidia driver/kernel on host as expected by the runtime libs in the container?

anil: driver 520.x on host, container has nvml libs from 520.x too.

mia: one more check: check the qdrep with `nsys stats out.qdrep --report=modules` and `nsys-ui` to inspect module load addresses. do the module base addresses line up with the host debugfile load addresses? if the debugfile's buildid matches but the absolute addresses don't line up, symbolizer won't find line numbers.

anil: ran `nsys stats` — modules list shows `/opt/runtime/lib/rt_kernels.so` loaded at 0x7f2a3e000000, but host debug file is for the same soname at a different preferred base (0x5609a000). is that expected?

chris: relocation / ASLR will change load base. symbolizers use relative addresses plus buildid mapping. but if nsys expects a separate debuglink file path and can't resolve buildid due to container pathmap restrictions, you get no lines. try setting `NSYS_USE_DEBuginfo=1` or `NSYS_CUPTI_VERBOSE=1` — iirc there are env flags documented in nsight profiler to enable host debug search.

anil: set `NSYS_USE_DEBuginfo=1` and reran — now we get partial lines for most kernels, but a few hot kernels still have `<unknown>` for some inlined frames.

mia: those remaining frames often come from device-inlined assembly or kernels JIT-ed/compiled at runtime (e.g., nvRTC or internally-assembled kernels). verify the runtime actually loads them from `rt_kernels.so` vs generating code at runtime. also check nvtx ranges to correlate.

perf-bot: automated job 1801234660 finished — attached perf.data for the same run at /artifacts/1801234660/perf.data

anil: looked at perf.data with `perf report -n --dsos=rt_kernels.so` and same missing lines. i ended up using `eu-unstrip --strip-debug` to reattach debug to the binary and restarted; that restored full line info in both nsys and perf.

chris: thanks — so it was a debuglink/objcopy packaging mismatch combined with nsight's stricter lookup rules inside containerized runs. can you add a small doc in eng-runtime troubleshooting with the minimal repro and the two workarounds (`NSYS_USE_DEBuginfo=1` and reattaching debug via eu-unstrip`) so others don't spend half a day?

anil: will do. i'll push a short runbook and a tiny script that verifies buildids and reattaches debug when packaging. saved the qdrep for the team. :thumbsup:
